decisions.reason: Direct presupposition from A's question 'What are you reading?' combined with the statement about B having nose buried in a book. B is clearly engaged in reading.

decisions.claim: B has been reading the book since last night
decisions.reason: Explicitly stated by A: 'You've had your nose buried in that book since last night.' Direct assertion about B's reading activity duration.

decisions.claim: B has not yet finished reading the book
decisions.reason: Necessary presupposition of 'Can I read it when you're finished?' — A assumes B has not yet finished, otherwise the request would be meaningless.

decisions.claim: B has knowledge of the book's content
decisions.reason: A says 'Don't tell me anything about it,' which presupposes B possesses knowledge of the book's content. This is a well-grounded inference from the request's presupposition structure.

decisions.claim: B is currently reading a book
decisions.reason: 'B is currently reading a book' is bidirectionally equivalent to 'B is reading a book' (c1). Same event, same granularity, no additional information.

decisions.claim: B started reading the book last night
decisions.reason: 'Since last night' in 'You've had your nose buried in that book since last night' most naturally implies B started reading last night. This is a grounded inference, though slight ambiguity exists (could have started earlier and been reading continuously since last night).
decisions.counterexample: B could have started reading the book before last night and continued reading it through last night into the present.

decisions.claim: B has not yet finished the book
decisions.reason: 'B has not yet finished the book' is bidirectionally equivalent to 'B has not yet finished reading the book' (c3). Same presupposition from the same turn, same granularity.
